title: Q3 2026 Earnings Preview: October 20-23, 2026 | META, TSLA, NFLX, GE, RTX
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/3t8olxuz1fwh1.jpg

# Key Points

* The October 20-23 earnings calendar spans 25 companies and offers unusually broad readings on artificial-intelligence investment, aerospace backlogs, consumer demand, credit quality, commodity markets and global industrial activity.
* Most companies are reporting calendar-third-quarter 2026 results, but Lam Research ([LRCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LRCX/)), Procter & Gamble ([PG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PG/)) and Western Digital ([WDC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/WDC/)) are expected to report fiscal first-quarter 2027 results.
* The technology focus falls on Meta Platforms ([META](https://tickeron.com/ticker/META/)), Tesla ([TSLA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TSLA/)) and Lam Research ([LRCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LRCX/)), where investors will judge whether AI-related revenue and demand justify sharply higher capital spending.
* Aerospace expectations are elevated after strong prior quarters from GE Aerospace ([GE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GE/)) and RTX ([RTX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RTX/)); execution against large commercial-services and defense backlogs will matter as much as headline EPS.
* Netflix ([NFLX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NFLX/)) and Spotify ([SPOT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SPOT/)) must show that advertising, pricing and subscriber monetization can support continued margin expansion without damaging engagement.
* Texas Instruments ([TXN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TXN/)), Western Digital ([WDC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/WDC/)) and Lam Research ([LRCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LRCX/)) will provide separate readings on the semiconductor cycle: analog demand, storage pricing and AI-driven wafer-fabrication spending.
* Defensive and cash-generative businesses—including Philip Morris International ([PM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PM/)), Procter & Gamble ([PG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PG/)), Chubb ([CB](https://tickeron.com/ticker/CB/)) and American Express ([AXP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AXP/))—face their own tests around pricing power, costs, catastrophe losses and consumer credit.
* Consensus estimates below are analyst forecasts, not yet-released company results. Company guidance is identified separately, and provider methodologies may produce modest differences in EPS and revenue expectations.

# Aerospace and Defense

Demand remains exceptionally strong across commercial aerospace and defense, but high backlogs have shifted the investment debate from order intake to execution. Engine deliveries, shop-visit throughput, parts availability, labor productivity and conversion of defense awards into revenue will determine whether these companies can sustain their current earnings momentum.

# Space Exploration Technologies

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. ([SPCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SPCX/)) is the least conventional name on the calendar and the one with the weakest consensus visibility. Public market data identify the company as SpaceX and show second-quarter revenue of approximately $7.81 billion, a quarterly loss of about $541 million and a preliminary third-quarter EPS estimate near $0.17, but major earnings calendars still display no standardized revenue or EPS forecast.

That discrepancy makes operating disclosure more important than a simple beat-or-miss calculation. Investors will want information on launch cadence, Starlink subscriber and revenue growth, terminal economics, satellite-production costs, capital expenditure and the cash demands of the Starship program. Given the company’s limited public reporting history, guidance quality and financial transparency could produce a larger valuation response than the reported EPS figure itself.

# GE Aerospace

GE Aerospace ([GE](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GE/)) enters its report after an unusually strong first half. Second-quarter adjusted revenue increased 24% to $12.6 billion, adjusted EPS reached $2.02 versus a $1.86 consensus, and management raised full-year EPS guidance to 7.65-7.85, operating-profit guidance to 10.55-10.75 billion and free-cash-flow guidance to 8.9-9.2 billion.

Consensus EPS for the third quarter is approximately $2.01. The central question is whether commercial-services growth can remain in the low-20% area while GE increases LEAP engine deliveries and works through supply-chain bottlenecks; management entered the quarter with more than 95% of expected spare-parts revenue already in backlog and roughly $170 billion of commercial-services backlog.

Analysts remain broadly constructive: the stock carries a Moderate Buy consensus, with 16 buys, three holds and one sell, and an average target near $386.67. A strong report would reinforce the long-duration aftermarket thesis, while any deterioration in margins, shop-visit throughput or free-cash-flow conversion could trigger a sharper response because expectations are already demanding.

# RTX Corporation

RTX Corporation ([RTX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RTX/)) is expected to report approximately $24.05 billion in revenue and 1.77-1.78 in EPS. The company delivered $24.71 billion of second-quarter revenue and $1.89 in adjusted EPS, and it subsequently guided to full-year adjusted EPS of 7.10-7.25.

Investors should concentrate on Collins Aerospace commercial aftermarket activity, Pratt & Whitney GTF installations and maintenance capacity, and Raytheon production rates for missile-defense systems. The size of the backlog supports multi-year visibility, but supply constraints and execution costs will determine how quickly that demand converts into cash and margin.

The analyst consensus is Moderate Buy, with 18 buys, eight holds and one sell and an average target around $226.75. Recent target reductions from RBC, Bernstein and TD Cowen suggest that analysts remain positive on fundamentals but are becoming more disciplined on valuation.

# Lockheed Martin

Lockheed Martin ([LMT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LMT/)) is expected to produce approximately $20.35 billion in revenue and $7.48 in EPS, representing projected growth of about 9% and 8%, respectively. The company beat expectations in the second quarter with $20.06 billion in revenue and $7.94 in EPS, then raised its 2026 outlook to 79.75-81.75 billion in sales and 29.95-30.65 in EPS.

The report will show whether missile-defense demand, international orders and a record backlog of roughly $230 billion can offset continuing execution risk on fixed-price development programs. Investors will also watch F-35 deliveries, classified-program performance and margins in Missiles and Fire Control.

Wall Street is divided rather than uniformly bullish: UBS has maintained a Buy view with a $653 target, while Barclays and TD Cowen have taken more neutral positions and Goldman Sachs has remained bearish. That split makes backlog conversion and any revision to full-year guidance especially important for the post-earnings reaction.

# Digital Media

The media reports will test whether streaming and social platforms can convert audience scale into durable profit growth. Advertising is a common swing factor, while rising content, infrastructure and AI costs make forward guidance more consequential than a small headline beat.

# Netflix

Netflix ([NFLX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NFLX/)) is expected to report roughly $12.88 billion in third-quarter revenue and $0.82 in EPS. Those estimates closely match company guidance of approximately 12.86-12.9 billion in revenue, 11.7%-12% growth and a 33.2% operating margin.

The company generated $12.56 billion in second-quarter revenue and $0.80 in EPS, with revenue slightly below consensus even as EPS edged past expectations. The forthcoming report therefore needs to demonstrate not only double-digit growth but also healthier engagement, continued pricing power and accelerating advertising revenue; management is targeting roughly $3 billion of advertising revenue for 2026.

Netflix carries a Moderate Buy consensus and an average target near $93.82, but several firms have recently reduced their targets because of softer engagement and currency concerns. An in-line quarter accompanied by cautious fourth-quarter guidance could disappoint, whereas advertising outperformance and sustained margin expansion would strengthen the case that the recent share-price weakness has discounted too much risk.

# Meta Platforms

Meta Platforms ([META](https://tickeron.com/ticker/META/)) faces one of the week’s highest-stakes reports. Consensus is centered near $63.2 billion in revenue and approximately $6.39 in EPS, against company revenue guidance of 61-64 billion.

The company’s second-quarter revenue increased 28% to approximately $60.8 billion, but EPS of $6.18 missed expectations as AI infrastructure spending pressured profitability. Operating margin fell to roughly 30.9%, quarterly capital expenditure reached $31.1 billion and full-year capital-expenditure guidance stands at 130-145 billion.

Investors will look for continued strength in advertising impressions and pricing, Family daily active people, Reels monetization and evidence that AI tools are improving ad conversion. Just as important will be any indication of 2027 expense growth: the stock’s recent history shows that strong advertising results can be overshadowed if spending guidance moves higher.

Wall Street nevertheless remains strongly positive, with a Moderate Buy consensus and an average target around $808.88; JPMorgan has maintained an Overweight rating and a $920 target. The earnings reaction will probably depend on whether management can connect its AI investment program to measurable revenue or engagement benefits rather than simply announcing another increase in infrastructure commitments.

# Spotify Technology

Spotify Technology ([SPOT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SPOT/)) has officially scheduled its third-quarter release for October 22 before the market opens, followed by an 8 a.m. ET question-and-answer session. Consensus calls for approximately €4.98 billion in revenue and €2.81 in EPS.

Second-quarter revenue reached €4.78 billion, Premium subscribers increased to 300 million, monthly active users reached 777 million and gross margin rose to a record 33.4%. Spotify guided for 788 million monthly active users, 305 million Premium subscribers, approximately €5 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 32.9% gross margin and €670 million of operating income.

The crucial issue is whether monetization can compensate for slower incremental user growth and continued weakness in advertising. Analysts retain a Moderate Buy consensus with an average target near $610, but recent downgrades and target reductions reflect concerns about label payments, advertising growth and the cost of new platform investments.

# Semiconductors and IT

This group provides a cross-section of the technology spending cycle. Lam Research ([LRCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LRCX/)) measures advanced-node and memory capital intensity, Texas Instruments ([TXN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TXN/)) tracks industrial and automotive demand, Western Digital ([WDC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/WDC/)) reflects storage pricing, while SAP ([SAP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SAP/)) and IBM ([IBM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IBM/)) test enterprise-software budgets.

# Lam Research

Lam Research ([LRCX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LRCX/)) is reporting fiscal first-quarter 2027 results, not calendar Q3 2026. Consensus stands near $8.13 billion in revenue and $2.18 in adjusted EPS, slightly above management’s guidance midpoint of $8.1 billion and $2.15.

The prior quarter produced record revenue of $6.72 billion and $1.82 in EPS, above the $1.69 consensus. The shares rallied sharply after that report, and the company has established a strong recent record of beating expectations.

The most important issue is December-quarter guidance. AI-driven investment in advanced logic, high-bandwidth memory and leading-edge packaging has created expectations that quarterly revenue could exceed $9 billion, so a mere September-quarter beat may not be sufficient. Analysts maintain a Moderate Buy consensus with an average target around $365, while several firms have targets approaching or above $400.

# Texas Instruments

Texas Instruments ([TXN](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TXN/)) is expected to report approximately $5.92 billion in revenue and $2.42 in EPS. Those figures sit comfortably within company guidance of 5.65-6.15 billion in revenue and 2.23-2.57 in EPS.

Second-quarter revenue increased 22.8% to $5.46 billion and EPS reached $2.14, beating the $1.91 consensus. Analog revenue grew 26%, while Embedded Processing revenue increased 16.1%, pointing to a broadening recovery from the semiconductor inventory correction.

The report should reveal whether industrial and automotive orders are normalizing sustainably or merely reflecting restocking. Investors will also examine factory utilization and the cash consequences of the company’s large domestic manufacturing program. Analyst views range from Hold to Moderate Buy depending on the provider, with broad-market consensus targets around 304-326 and a bullish $400 target from KeyBanc.

# Western Digital

Western Digital ([WDC](https://tickeron.com/ticker/WDC/)) is scheduled to report fiscal first-quarter 2027 results after the October 22 close. Consensus calls for approximately 4.14-4.16 billion in revenue and 4.07-4.08 in EPS, compared with company guidance of 4.0-4.2 billion and $4.00 plus or minus $0.15.

The company expects a non-GAAP gross margin of 55%-56%, making margin performance at least as important as the top line. Investors will focus on cloud hard-disk demand, capacity pricing, data-center storage investment and the durability of the earnings recovery after four consecutive quarterly EPS beats.

Because consensus sits close to the upper half of management’s revenue range, guidance for the December quarter may drive the stock more forcefully than the reported fiscal first-quarter numbers. Any indication that storage pricing is peaking would challenge expectations embedded in projected fiscal 2027 EPS growth.

# SAP SE

SAP SE ([SAP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SAP/)) is expected to report approximately €10.10 billion in Q3 revenue and about €1.68 in GAAP EPS. Consensus anticipates cloud-revenue growth of roughly 24%, making current cloud backlog and cloud gross margin the central operating indicators.

At the prior update, current cloud backlog increased 27% and cloud revenue rose 22%, while SAP maintained 2026 cloud-revenue guidance of €25.8-€26.2 billion at constant currencies. The company trimmed its non-IFRS operating-profit outlook to €11.8-€12.2 billion to reflect the dilutive effects of recently completed acquisitions.

Analyst sentiment remains favorable: SAP carries a Moderate Buy consensus and an average target around $264.71. The stock’s response will likely depend on whether cloud-backlog momentum remains near the mid-20% range and whether management can show that AI-related hiring and computing costs are temporary rather than a structural margin headwind.

# IBM

International Business Machines Corporation ([IBM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IBM/)) is expected to report about $16.82 billion in revenue and $2.86 in adjusted EPS. The company’s second quarter produced $17.16 billion in revenue and $2.93 in adjusted EPS, but sales fell short of expectations and management reduced full-year constant-currency revenue-growth guidance to 4%-5%.

Software growth, consulting signings and mainframe-related transaction-processing revenue will be the decisive metrics. IBM expects full-year software growth of 6%-8% and continues to target roughly $1 billion of year-over-year free-cash-flow growth, but the second-quarter shortfall has increased the burden on the final two quarters.

The analyst consensus is Moderate Buy, with an average target near $255, although several current targets sit only modestly above the share price. Investors therefore need evidence that delayed enterprise deals are converting, organic software growth is improving and free cash flow remains intact after substantial acquisition spending.

# Healthcare

Medical technology and life-science tools are emerging from different demand environments. Intuitive Surgical ([ISRG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ISRG/)) is benefiting from procedure and installed-base expansion, while Thermo Fisher Scientific ([TMO](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TMO/)) must confirm that the biopharma and laboratory-equipment recovery is broadening.

# Intuitive Surgical

Intuitive Surgical ([ISRG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ISRG/)) is expected to report approximately $2.88 billion in revenue and $2.61 in EPS, representing projected growth of roughly 15% and 9%, respectively. The company has exceeded EPS estimates in each of the last four reported quarters, including second-quarter EPS of $2.80 against a $2.51 consensus.

Investors will focus on da Vinci procedure growth, new-system placements, the installed base, instruments-and-accessories revenue and adoption of the da Vinci 5 platform. Management has guided to 13.5%-15.5% full-year procedure growth, with international activity recently outpacing the U.S.

The stock carries a Moderate Buy consensus and an average target around $499, although individual targets range widely because of debate over its premium valuation. A strong procedure number accompanied by healthy recurring revenue would support that valuation; weakness in U.S. procedures, China pricing or gross margin would make the multiple more difficult to defend.

# Thermo Fisher Scientific

Thermo Fisher Scientific ([TMO](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TMO/)) is expected to produce approximately $11.9 billion in revenue and $6.40 in adjusted EPS. The company previously reported $11.99 billion in quarterly revenue and $6.03 in adjusted EPS, then raised full-year guidance to 47.4-48.1 billion in revenue and 24.93-25.33 in adjusted EPS.

The report will test whether improving pharmaceutical and biotechnology demand is translating into sustained organic growth across laboratory products, analytical instruments and bioproduction. Investors should distinguish acquisition and currency contributions from underlying volume growth and watch whether margins improve alongside demand.

Wall Street remains constructive, with a Moderate Buy consensus and an average target around $654, although recent targets have been raised as high as $760. Because the shares have already re-rated, a routine beat may have limited impact unless management also raises guidance or describes a stronger recovery into 2027.

# Financials

This group covers three different financial cycles: catastrophe and commercial pricing at Chubb ([CB](https://tickeron.com/ticker/CB/)), realizations and fundraising at Blackstone ([BX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/BX/)), and premium-consumer spending and credit at American Express ([AXP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AXP/)).

# Chubb Limited

Chubb Limited ([CB](https://tickeron.com/ticker/CB/)) is expected to release results after the October 20 close, with its conference call scheduled for the following morning. Current estimates call for approximately $16.72 billion in revenue and $6.42 in EPS.

The company’s second-quarter core operating EPS increased to $7.26 and exceeded consensus by about 9.5%, while revenue reached approximately $15.77 billion. For Q3, the combined ratio is expected to rise to roughly 87.2% from 81.8% a year earlier, reflecting a less favorable catastrophe comparison.

Net premiums written, commercial-property pricing, catastrophe losses and investment income will determine earnings quality. An EPS beat driven by reserve releases would be less persuasive than one supported by premium growth and resilient underlying underwriting margins.

# Blackstone

Blackstone ([BX](https://tickeron.com/ticker/BX/)) is expected to report approximately 3.35-3.36 billion in revenue and 1.29-1.31 in distributable EPS. Consensus also looks for total assets under management of about $1.38 trillion and fee-earning assets under management near $982 billion.

Management fees are expected to grow, but performance-related revenue and realizations remain sensitive to exit markets. Investors will watch fundraising, deployment, private-credit growth, real-estate valuations and whether lower financing costs are beginning to improve transaction activity.

Analysts maintain a Moderate Buy consensus, with an average target of approximately $144, but recent target cuts indicate caution around realizations and near-term earnings visibility. A recovery in asset sales or stronger fee-related earnings would support the stock; another subdued realization quarter could keep attention on the timing rather than the size of long-term embedded performance revenue.

# American Express

American Express Company ([AXP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/AXP/)) is expected to report approximately $20.13 billion in revenue and $4.47 in EPS, implying projected growth of 9.3% and 8%, respectively. Full-year consensus stands near $79.47 billion in revenue and $17.65 in EPS.

The operating indicators will include network volumes, billed business, net interest income, card-fee growth, provisions and delinquency trends. Consensus calls for network volumes to increase 8.6%, U.S. Consumer Services billed business to rise 9.6% and the average fee per card to increase 12.3%.

American Express is still benefiting from its affluent customer base and fee-rich premium products, but higher marketing expenses and normalization in credit costs could limit operating leverage. RBC recently maintained an Outperform rating while lowering its target to $400 from $415, illustrating a still-positive but increasingly valuation-conscious analyst stance.

# Consumer and Autos

Pricing power is the connecting theme across this group. Tesla ([TSLA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TSLA/)) must defend automotive economics while financing major AI projects; Philip Morris International ([PM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PM/)) must sustain smoke-free-product growth; and Procter & Gamble ([PG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PG/)) must balance volume recovery against input-cost inflation.

# Tesla

Tesla ([TSLA](https://tickeron.com/ticker/TSLA/)) is expected to report approximately $27.9 billion in revenue and 0.44-0.45 in EPS. The company delivered 486,532 vehicles during Q3, above the company-compiled consensus of 461,974, but deliveries declined about 2% year over year and exceeded production by more than 22,000 units.

That gap makes automotive gross margin and free cash flow more important than the delivery headline. Second-quarter revenue reached $28.24 billion, but EPS of $0.33 missed expectations; projected capital expenditure above $25 billion for Cybercab, Optimus, AI chips and manufacturing capacity creates an additional cash-flow hurdle.

Management’s comments on robotaxi deployment, Full Self-Driving, Optimus production and lower-cost vehicles may influence the shares more than quarterly EPS. Analysts remain sharply divided: one broad survey assigns a Hold consensus and an average target of $412.33, with individual targets ranging from $25.28 to $840. That dispersion reflects the stock’s central debate—whether it should be valued mainly as an automaker or as an emerging autonomy and robotics platform.

# Philip Morris International

Philip Morris International ([PM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PM/)) is expected to report roughly $11.42 billion in revenue and $2.31 in EPS, implying projected growth of about 5% and 3%. The company delivered $11.19 billion in second-quarter revenue and $2.20 in EPS, both above expectations.

Investors should monitor shipment growth and margins for IQOS and ZYN, the geographic mix of smoke-free products, currency effects and whether traditional cigarette pricing continues to offset volume declines. The long-term investment case increasingly depends on smoke-free revenue growth translating into higher consolidated margins and cash flow.

The stock carries an Overweight-to-Moderate Buy consensus, with average targets around 207-211. Because the shares recently approached a 52-week high, guidance and the quality of volume growth will matter more than a small EPS beat.

# Procter & Gamble

The Procter & Gamble Company ([PG](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PG/)) will report fiscal first-quarter 2027 results rather than calendar Q3 2026. Consensus is approximately $22.7 billion in revenue and 1.88-1.89 in core EPS, implying modest sales growth but an earnings decline of roughly 5%.

Management has guided to fiscal 2027 organic-sales growth of 1%-3% and core EPS of 6.89-7.11, while flagging significant commodity, energy and transportation headwinds. The report will show whether improving U.S. consumption and pricing can offset cost pressure and softer demand in selected international markets.

Analyst opinion is moderately positive but not unanimous, with consensus targets generally around 158-162. The most market-sensitive figures will be organic volume, price/mix and gross margin: stronger volume with stable guidance would support the defensive-growth thesis, while renewed volume weakness could revive concerns that years of pricing have reached their limit.

# Transportation

# Union Pacific

Union Pacific Corporation ([UNP](https://tickeron.com/ticker/UNP/)) is expected to report approximately $7.08 billion in revenue and 3.45-3.47 in EPS. The company has recently exceeded EPS expectations, including second-quarter EPS of $3.41 versus a $3.26 estimate.

The quarter will provide a reading on freight volumes, pricing, fuel expenses, labor productivity and the operating ratio. Investors will also look for updates on the proposed Norfolk Southern combination, including regulatory milestones, integration spending and management’s estimated potential to shift freight from road to rail.

For the stock, the distinction between cost-driven and volume-driven earnings growth is crucial. A lower operating ratio accompanied by improving carloads would indicate a healthier freight cycle, while earnings supported mainly by cost reductions could leave investors cautious about the underlying economy.

# Energy and Materials

Oilfield activity, refining margins and gold prices make this the most commodity-sensitive group. The earnings figures may be strong, but investor reactions will depend heavily on management’s forward assumptions for margins, regional activity, production and capital returns.

# Valero Energy

Valero Energy Corporation ([VLO](https://tickeron.com/ticker/VLO/)) is expected to report approximately $38.8 billion in revenue and $21.23 in EPS. The EPS forecast implies an extraordinary year-over-year increase, reflecting strong refining margins and tight product markets.

Investors should examine refining throughput, utilization, capture rates, operating expenses and performance in renewable diesel and ethanol. A large accounting beat will matter less if management indicates that product cracks and industry utilization are beginning to normalize.

Estimate revisions have been predominantly positive, and one earnings-ranking methodology currently assigns the stock its strongest rating. Still, the high consensus bar means the market may demand both an earnings beat and constructive commentary on fourth-quarter margins.

# Newmont

Newmont Corporation ([NEM](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NEM/)) is expected to report approximately $6.01 billion in revenue and 1.95-1.96 in EPS. Second-quarter EPS of $2.10 exceeded consensus, while the company generated approximately $5.3 billion of free cash flow during the first half.

Higher realized gold prices are supportive, but production and costs will determine how much of that benefit reaches shareholders. Newmont expects 2026 gold production of about 5.26 million ounces and all-in sustaining costs of approximately $1,680 per ounce, with sequentially higher third-quarter unit costs anticipated.

Analyst sentiment remains constructive, with an Overweight consensus and an average target around $139. The strongest outcome would combine stable production, controlled costs and additional capital returns; a cost-driven miss could prompt investors to question operating leverage despite the favorable gold-price environment.

# SLB

SLB N.V. ([SLB](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLB/)) is expected to report approximately $9.27 billion in revenue and $0.62 in adjusted EPS. Second-quarter revenue reached $8.97 billion and adjusted EPS was $0.55, while adjusted EBITDA totaled $1.90 billion and free cash flow was $716 million.

Management previously projected 3%-4% sequential Q3 revenue growth and approximately 75 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion, assuming gradual recovery in the Middle East. Regional activity, ChampionX integration, Production Systems margins and Digital revenue will therefore be the most important checkpoints.

The company also continues to target more than $4 billion of 2026 shareholder distributions while carrying net debt of approximately $8.7 billion. Analysts maintain a Moderate Buy consensus, with 24 buys, two holds and one sell and an average target around $62.35.

For investors, the report must establish that international recovery and Digital growth can outweigh uneven upstream spending. A result near consensus with improving margins and Middle East activity would support the recovery narrative; weak guidance or slower integration progress would shift attention back to leverage and oil-service cyclicality.
